walk.action: A genuine in-place six-phase humanoid walk cycle in the accepted right-facing three-quarter camera. The attached single curated idle frame is the ONLY identity source: retain its bell helmet, amber eyes, charcoal plain underclothes, brown gloves and boots. Empty hands, no armor, no weapon, no cape. Keep the pelvis centered in each slot; ground progression belongs to the future engine, not shifting identical cutouts across slots. Near means camera-near leg/arm and far means camera-far leg/arm; keep each limb role throughout the cycle. Natural opposite arm/leg swing. At least one real stance foot or toe touches the same ground baseline in every pose, no airborne running. All six poses must have distinct knee/ankle/foot-contact relationships. Pose 1 (near_contact): support near heel accepts weight; far toe is ending rear support; near foot forward toward screen-right, heel down, toe slightly lifted; far foot behind toward screen-left, rear toe down, heel raised; arms near arm back; far arm forward; empty gloves open/relaxed; body soft contact compression through knees; rigid helmet keeps shape. Pose 2 (near_support_far_pass): support near sole flat under body; far foot clearly off ground; near foot weight-bearing stance foot moves backward relative to hips; far foot bent knee swings forward passing beneath pelvis, boot clears floor; arms arms pass through neutral; elbows remain recognizable; body pelvis rises slightly on near support; helmet translates as one rigid unit. Pose 3 (near_push_far_reach): support near rear toe still contacts; far leading heel is about to land; near foot behind pelvis, heel lifts for push-off; far foot extends forward with raised toe, not yet a second planted sole; arms near arm continues toward front as near leg travels back; far arm back; body small controlled weight transfer, no airborne run phase. Pose 4 (far_contact): support far heel accepts weight; near toe ends rear support; near foot behind toward screen-left, rear toe down, heel raised; far foot forward toward screen-right, heel down, toe slightly lifted; arms near arm forward; far arm back; opposite contact to frame0; body opposite contact compression; do not duplicate or flip the whole sprite. Pose 5 (far_support_near_pass): support far sole flat under body; near foot clearly off ground; near foot bent knee swings forward passing beneath pelvis, boot clears floor; far foot weight-bearing stance foot moves backward relative to hips; arms opposite passing phase to frame1; two hands remain distinct; body pelvis rises slightly on far support; same rigid helmet scale. Pose 6 (far_push_near_reach): support far rear toe still contacts; near leading heel is about to land; near foot extends forward to prepare the next frame0 heel contact; far foot behind pelvis, heel lifts for push-off; arms near arm heads back; far arm forward, preparing frame0; body flows into frame0 with no reset, body teleport or repeated contact pose. The bell helmet is rigid metal: keep its exact width, height, visor opening, two eye shapes, hinge/rivet and top knob across all poses. No helmet squash, shortening, perspective drift, blinking or changing eye count. Permit only a small coherent rigid head translation (at most about 6 source-pixel vertical range); knee/hip motion must carry the gait. Keep limb lengths, hand size, glove shape and boot identity stable. Preserve a visible separation of swing and stance feet, and near/far arm silhouettes where possible. Close the sixth-to-first seam through near heel contact; do not append a seventh pose or duplicate an idle pose. Same illustration scale, stable in-slot pelvis and complete head-to-toe silhouette within all safe margins. No dust, shadows, trails, FX, scenery, text, slot borders or labels in the art.
